s: 这是爸爸买得足球。
s_py: zhè shì bà bà mǎi de zú qiú
zh: 这是爸爸买的足球。
py: zhè shì bà bà mǎi de zú qiú
en: This is the football Dad bought.
why: 买 + 足球 is a clause describing a noun, so 的. 得 would need a judgement or result after it, not a noun.

s: 这是我哥哥买的球鞋。
s_py: zhè shì wǒ gē gē mǎi de qiú xié
zh: 这是我哥哥买的球鞋。
py: zhè shì wǒ gē gē mǎi de qiú xié
en: These are the sneakers my older brother bought.
why: 买 is followed by 的 because the noun 球鞋 follows. The verb before the de does not force 得.

s: 在公园里打太极拳得那些老人每天早上六点就到了。
s_py: zài gōng yuán lǐ dǎ tài jí quán de nà xiē lǎo rén měi tiān zǎo shàng liù diǎn jiù dào le
zh: 在公园里打太极拳的那些老人每天早上六点就到了。
py: zài gōng yuán lǐ dǎ tài jí quán de nà xiē lǎo rén měi tiān zǎo shàng liù diǎn jiù dào le
en: The old people who do tai chi in the park are there every morning at six.
why: The clause 在公园里打太极拳 describes the noun phrase 那些老人, so 的. 得 would need to follow a verb and be followed by a judgement.

q: 你们走___太慢了，我们要迟到了。
zh: 你们走得太慢了，我们要迟到了。
py: nǐ men zǒu de tài màn le wǒ men yào chí dào le
en: You walk too slowly, we are going to be late.
why: 走 is the verb and 太慢了 is the judgement, so 得 sits between them. 的 would need a noun after it.

q: 地铁站在那个很大___公园旁边。
zh: 地铁站在那个很大的公园旁边。
py: dì tiě zhàn zài nà ge hěn dà de gōng yuán páng biān
en: The metro station is next to that very big park.
why: 很大 describes the noun 公园, so the link is 的. 地 would need a verb right after it, and 得 needs a verb or adjective before it as its base.

q: 站在这儿就能看___见前面的体育馆。
zh: 站在这儿就能看得见前面的体育馆。
py: zhàn zài zhè r jiù néng kàn de jiàn qián miàn de tǐ yù guǎn
en: From here you can see the gymnasium ahead.
why: Verb + 得 + result word means 'can': 看得见. 不 would say you cannot see it, contradicting 能. 的 would need a noun after it.

q: 你慢慢___说，我听不懂。
zh: 你慢慢地说，我听不懂。
py: nǐ màn màn de shuō wǒ tīng bù dǒng
en: Speak slowly; I don't understand.
why: 慢慢 is a doubled adjective in front of the verb 说, so 地. The doubling does not change the rule: position decides.

q: 我弟弟踢足球___比我好多了。
zh: 我弟弟踢足球踢得比我好多了。
py: wǒ dì di tī zú qiú tī de bǐ wǒ hǎo duō le
en: My younger brother plays football much better than I do.
why: The object 足球 sits after 踢, so 踢 is said again and 得 follows it. A bare 得 after the object is not possible.

s: 小李开车得很稳。
s_py: xiǎo lǐ kāi chē de hěn wěn
zh: 小李开车开得很稳。
py: xiǎo lǐ kāi chē kāi de hěn wěn
en: Xiao Li drives very steadily.
why: 得 attached to the object 车 is wrong. The verb is repeated: 开车开得很稳.

q: 他很流利___回答了裁判的问题。
zh: 他很流利地回答了裁判的问题。
py: tā hěn liú lì de huí dá le cái pàn de wèn tí
en: He answered the referee's questions very fluently.
why: 很流利 describes how he answered, and 回答 follows, so 地. 得 would need 回答 to come first.

q: 昨天的足球赛，他们踢___不好，输了比赛。
zh: 昨天的足球赛，他们踢得不好，输了比赛。
py: zuó tiān de zú qiú sài tā men tī de bù hǎo shū le bǐ sài
en: In yesterday's football match they played badly and lost.
why: 踢得不好 negates the judgement, not the verb: 不 goes after 得. 的 would need a noun after it, and 地 a verb.

s: 我昨天跑得很累，今天腿疼得走不了路。
s_py: wǒ zuó tiān pǎo de tài lèi jīn tiān tuǐ téng de zǒu bù liǎo lù
zh: 我昨天跑得很累，今天腿疼得走不了路。
py: wǒ zuó tiān pǎo de hěn lèi jīn tiān tuǐ téng de zǒu bù liǎo lù
en: I got very tired from running yesterday, and today my legs hurt so much that I can't walk.
why: 跑得很累 is a judgement of the running and 疼得走不了路 is a 'so ... that' result, so both are 得. Correct.

q: 我昨天买___球鞋很贵。
zh: 我昨天买的球鞋很贵。
py: wǒ zuó tiān mǎi de qiú xié hěn guì
en: The sneakers I bought yesterday were expensive.
why: The gap follows the verb 买, which tempts 得, but the noun 球鞋 comes right after it. A clause that describes a noun is joined with 的.

q: 我看___懂这个字，你能教我吗？
zh: 我看不懂这个字，你能教我吗？
py: wǒ kàn bù dǒng zhè ge zì nǐ néng jiào wǒ ma
en: I can't read this character; can you teach me?
why: The cue and the request for help mean 'cannot', so 得 is swapped for 不: 看不懂. 看得懂 would mean the opposite.

s: 他们高高兴兴地去爬山了。
s_py: tā men gāo gāo xìng xìng de qù pá shān le
zh: 他们高高兴兴地去爬山了。
py: tā men gāo gāo xìng xìng de qù pá shān le
en: They went off climbing in high spirits.
why: The doubled adjective in front of the verb 去 takes 地, so the sentence is correct.

s: 裁判认真得看了一遍录像，然后改了决定。
s_py: cái pàn rèn zhēn de kàn le yī biàn lù xiàng rán hòu gǎi le jué dìng
zh: 裁判认真地看了一遍录像，然后改了决定。
py: cái pàn rèn zhēn de kàn le yī biàn lù xiàng rán hòu gǎi le jué dìng
en: The referee watched the replay carefully and then changed the decision.
why: 认真 describes the manner of the verb 看, so it takes 地. 得 cannot sit before a verb of the action.

s: 我们慢慢得走回家。
s_py: wǒ men màn màn de zǒu huí jiā
zh: 我们慢慢地走回家。
py: wǒ men màn màn de zǒu huí jiā
en: We walked slowly home.
why: 慢慢 describes the manner of 走, so it needs 地 before the verb. 得 only follows a verb or adjective.

s: 路上的车太多，我们开得很慢。
s_py: lù shàng de chē tài duō wǒ men kāi de hěn màn
zh: 路上的车太多，我们开得很慢。
py: lù shàng de chē tài duō wǒ men kāi de hěn màn
en: There was too much traffic on the road, so we drove very slowly.
why: 开 + 得 + 很慢 judges how we drove, with no object, so no repeated verb is needed. Correct.

q: 请你清楚___告诉我地铁站怎么走。
zh: 请你清楚地告诉我地铁站怎么走。
py: qǐng nǐ qīng chǔ de gào sù wǒ dì tiě zhàn zěn me zǒu
en: Please tell me clearly how to get to the metro station.
why: 清楚 is the manner of the verb 告诉, so 地. 得 needs a verb on its left, and 请你 cannot take it.

zh: 他游泳游得很快。
py: tā yóu yǒng yóu de hěn kuài
en: He swims fast.
why: 得 follows the repeated verb 游, not the object 游泳. The object can also be fronted as a topic.

s: 他说话太快，我不听得懂。
s_py: tā shuō huà tài kuài wǒ bù tīng de dǒng
zh: 他说话太快，我听不懂。
py: tā shuō huà tài kuài wǒ tīng bù dǒng
en: He speaks too fast, and I cannot understand.
why: To say 'cannot', 得 becomes 不: 听不懂. A 不 in front of 听得懂 is a classic mistake that natives do not make.

s: 这是一个很大地公园。
s_py: zhè shì yí gè hěn dà de gōng yuán
zh: 这是一个很大的公园。
py: zhè shì yī gè hěn dà de gōng yuán
en: This is a very big park.
why: The noun 公园 follows, so a describing word takes 的. 地 is only for linking to a verb.

q: 他是我们队里最高___球员。
zh: 他是我们队里最高的球员。
py: tā shì wǒ men duì lǐ zuì gāo de qiú yuán
en: He is the tallest player on our team.
why: 最高 describes the noun 球员, so 的 is the link. 地 would be wrong because no verb follows.

s: 我不看得懂这个路牌。
s_py: wǒ bù kàn de dǒng zhè ge lù pái
zh: 我看不懂这个路牌。
py: wǒ kàn bù dǒng zhè ge lù pái
en: I can't understand this road sign.
why: The 'cannot' form swaps 得 for 不 inside the verb: 看不懂. Putting 不 before the verb and keeping 得 is not Chinese.

q: 前面那条路___名字叫中山路。
zh: 前面那条路的名字叫中山路。
py: qián miàn nà tiáo lù de míng zì jiào zhōng shān lù
en: The name of the road ahead is Zhongshan Road.
why: 路 and 名字 are both nouns and the road owns the name, so 的 links them. 地 and 得 never sit between two nouns.

s: 弟弟不跑得快。
s_py: dì di bù pǎo de kuài
zh: 弟弟跑得不快。
py: dì di pǎo de bù kuài
en: My younger brother doesn't run fast.
why: With 得, the negative goes on the judgement: 跑得不快. 不 before the verb is not possible in this pattern.

q: 他是一个很努力___运动员。
zh: 他是一个很努力的运动员。
py: tā shì yī gè hěn nǔ lì de yùn dòng yuán
en: He is a very hardworking athlete.
why: 努力 sits before the noun 运动员, so 的. The same word before a verb would take 地 and after a verb 得.

q: 我们安安静静___坐在球场边，看着他们比赛。
zh: 我们安安静静地坐在球场边，看着他们比赛。
py: wǒ men ān ān jìng jìng de zuò zài qiú chǎng biān kàn zhe tā men bǐ sài
en: We sat quietly at the edge of the pitch, watching them play.
why: 安安静静 gives the manner of 坐, so 地 sits between them. 得 would need 坐 before it.

q: 她今天来___很早。
zh: 她今天来得很早。
py: tā jīn tiān lái de hěn zǎo
en: She came very early today.
why: 来 + 得 + 很早 judges how early she came. 地 would need a verb after it, and 的 a noun.

q: 他练球练___很努力，所以进步很快。
zh: 他练球练得很努力，所以进步很快。
py: tā liàn qiú liàn de hěn nǔ lì suǒ yǐ jìn bù hěn kuài
en: He trains very hard, so he improves quickly.
why: 练 is repeated before 得, and 很努力 judges how he trains. 地 would belong before the verb, not after it.

s: 你看得见那个路牌吗？
s_py: nǐ kàn de jiàn nà ge lù pái ma
zh: 你看得见那个路牌吗？
py: nǐ kàn de jiàn nà ge lù pái ma
en: Can you see that road sign?
why: 看得见 is the positive 'can see' form, and the question is formed with 吗. Correct.

q: 他的字写___工工整整。
zh: 他的字写得工工整整。
py: tā de zì xiě de gōng gōng zhěng zhěng
en: His characters are written very neatly.
why: 写 is the verb and 工工整整 describes the result, so 得 follows 写 even though the adjective is doubled. 地 is for before a verb.

q: 今天热___我不想出门。
zh: 今天热得我不想出门。
py: jīn tiān rè de wǒ bù xiǎng chū mén
en: It's so hot today that I don't want to go out.
why: 热 + 得 + result clause, with its own subject 我. 地 would need a verb right after it, but 我 is a subject.

q: 队员们互相鼓励，努力___爬到了山顶。
zh: 队员们互相鼓励，努力地爬到了山顶。
py: duì yuán men hù xiāng gǔ lì nǔ lì de pá dào le shān dǐng
en: The team members encouraged one another and climbed to the summit with great effort.
why: 努力 is the manner of the verb 爬到, so 地 comes before it. 得 would follow a verb, and there is none before 努力.

q: 我们高高兴兴___骑车去了公园。
zh: 我们高高兴兴地骑车去了公园。
py: wǒ men gāo gāo xìng xìng de qí chē qù le gōng yuán
en: We cheerfully rode our bikes to the park.
why: 高高兴兴 is a doubled description of how we rode, in front of the verb 骑, so 地. 得 would need a verb before it.

s: 她游泳游得比我快多了。
s_py: tā yóu yǒng yóu de bǐ wǒ kuài duō le
zh: 她游泳游得比我快多了。
py: tā yóu yǒng yóu de bǐ wǒ kuài duō le
en: She swims much faster than I do.
why: The verb 游 is repeated after 游泳 and 得 follows it. A 比 phrase can sit inside the judgement.

q: 我们昨天晚上在街角吃___那家面馆下个月要搬走了。
zh: 我们昨天晚上在街角吃的那家面馆下个月要搬走了。
py: wǒ men zuó tiān wǎn shàng zài jiē jiǎo chī de nà jiā miàn guǎn xià gè yuè yào bān zǒu le
en: The noodle shop on the corner where we ate last night will move away next month.
why: 吃 is followed by the noun phrase 那家面馆, which the whole clause describes. 得 after 吃 would need a judgement such as 很饱 directly after it.

s: 足球他踢得很好。
s_py: zú qiú tā tī de hěn hǎo
zh: 足球他踢得很好。
py: zú qiú tā tī de hěn hǎo
en: He plays football very well.
why: The object 足球 is moved to the front as the topic, so 踢 needs no repeating and 得 follows it directly. This is fully correct.

q: 弟弟在公园拍___那张照片很漂亮。
zh: 弟弟在公园拍的那张照片很漂亮。
py: dì di zài gōng yuán pāi de nà zhāng zhào piān hěn piào liàng
en: The photo my younger brother took in the park is beautiful.
why: 拍 is a verb, but the next word begins the noun phrase 那张照片. Verb + 的 + noun marks 'the photo that was taken', not 拍得 + judgement.

q: 这是爸爸开___车。
zh: 这是爸爸开的车。
py: zhè shì bà bà kāi de chē
en: This is the car Dad drives.
why: 开 is a verb, but 车 is the noun it describes: 爸爸开的车 means 'the car Dad drives'. 得 would need a judgement like 很快 after it.

s: 我听不懂他说的话。
s_py: wǒ tīng bù dǒng tā shuō de huà
zh: 我听不懂他说的话。
py: wǒ tīng bù dǒng tā shuō de huà
en: I can't understand what he says.
why: 听不懂 is the 'cannot' form of 听得懂. 说的话 is a clause plus 的 plus a noun. Both uses are correct.

q: 这么多菜，我们三个人肯定吃___完。
zh: 这么多菜，我们三个人肯定吃不完。
py: zhè me duō cài wǒ men sān gè rén kěn dìng chī bù wán
en: With this much food, the three of us definitely cannot finish it.
why: 吃 + result word 完, and 肯定 with 这么多菜 means 'cannot'. 不 replaces 得. 吃得完 would claim we can.

q: 孩子轻轻___把门关上了。
zh: 孩子轻轻地把门关上了。
py: hái zi qīng qīng de bǎ mén guān shàng le
en: The child closed the door gently.
why: 轻轻 describes how the door was closed and the verb phrase follows, so 地. 得 needs a verb on its left.

zh: 我们认真地看地图。
py: wǒ men rèn zhēn de kàn dì tú
en: We looked at the map carefully.
why: 认真 + 地 sits before the verb 看 and cannot follow it. The judgement pattern would be 看得很认真.

s: 今天风大地让我们没法骑车。
s_py: jīn tiān fēng dà de ràng wǒ men méi fǎ qí chē
zh: 今天风大得让我们没法骑车。
py: jīn tiān fēng dà de ràng wǒ men méi fǎ qí chē
en: The wind is so strong today that we can't ride our bikes.
why: 风大 is a state and 让我们没法骑车 is its result, so it is 得. 地 would need a verb of manner to follow.

q: 虽然他刚学滑冰，但是滑___已经很稳了。
zh: 虽然他刚学滑冰，但是滑得已经很稳了。
py: suī rán tā gāng xué huá bīng dàn shì huá de yǐ jīng hěn wěn le
en: Although he has only just learned to skate, he already skates quite steadily.
why: 滑 is the verb and 已经很稳了 is the judgement of how he skates, so 得. 地 would put a manner before a verb, not after one.

q: 我们在体育馆看___那场比赛很精彩。
zh: 我们在体育馆看的那场比赛很精彩。
py: wǒ men zài tǐ yù guǎn kàn de nà chǎng bǐ sài hěn jīng cǎi
en: The match we watched at the gymnasium was exciting.
why: After 看 comes the noun phrase 那场比赛, so the clause 我们在体育馆看 is describing it and needs 的. 得 would need an adjective or result after it.

q: 冬天的风冷___让人睁不开眼睛。
zh: 冬天的风冷得让人睁不开眼睛。
py: dōng tiān de fēng lěng de ràng rén zhēng bù kāi yǎn jīng
en: The winter wind is so cold that you can't open your eyes.
why: 冷 + 得 + 让人睁不开眼睛 is 'so cold that ...'. 的 would need a noun, and 地 a verb, but a result clause follows.

q: 票已经卖完了，我们肯定买___到了。
zh: 票已经卖完了，我们肯定买不到了。
py: piào yǐ jīng mài wán le wǒ men kěn dìng mǎi bù dào le
en: The tickets are sold out, so we definitely cannot get any now.
why: 卖完了 means none are left, so we 'cannot' buy: 买不到. 得 would claim success, which the first clause rules out.

q: 司机耐心___等着乘客上车。
zh: 司机耐心地等着乘客上车。
py: sī jī nài xīn de děng zhe chéng kè shàng chē
en: The driver patiently waited for the passengers to get on.
why: 耐心 is the manner of the action 等着, so 耐心 + 地 + verb. 得 would turn the verb 等着 into the base of a judgement, which is not what the order says.

q: 站在山顶上，我们看___到整个城市，真漂亮！
zh: 站在山顶上，我们看得到整个城市，真漂亮！
py: zhàn zài shān dǐng shàng wǒ men kàn de dào zhěng gè chéng shì zhēn piào liang
en: Standing on the summit, we can see the whole city, it's beautiful!
why: Verb + 得 + 到 means 'can see'; the delight in 真漂亮 shows the view is open to us. 看不到 would say the opposite, and 的 would need a noun after it.

q: 她唱歌___很好听。
zh: 她唱歌唱得很好听。
py: tā chàng gē chàng de hěn hǎo tīng
en: She sings beautifully.
why: The verb 唱 is repeated after the object 歌, then 得. 唱歌得 puts 得 after the object, which is not allowed.

q: 他跑___很快。
zh: 他跑得很快。
py: tā pǎo de hěn kuài
en: He runs fast.
why: 跑 is a verb and 很快 judges how he runs, so 得 goes between them. 的 needs a noun after it and 地 needs a verb after it.

q: 这是我哥哥___足球。
zh: 这是我哥哥的足球。
py: zhè shì wǒ gē gē de zú qiú
en: This is my older brother's football.
why: 哥哥 is the owner and 足球 is a noun, so 的 joins them. 得 follows a verb or adjective and 地 sits before a verb; neither can link an owner to a noun.

s: 他很快地跑到球场中间，把球传给了队友。
s_py: tā hěn kuài de pǎo dào qiú chǎng zhōng jiān bǎ qiú chuán gěi le duì yǒu
zh: 他很快地跑到球场中间，把球传给了队友。
py: tā hěn kuài de pǎo dào qiú chǎng zhōng jiān bǎ qiú chuán gěi le duì yǒu
en: He quickly ran to the middle of the pitch and passed the ball to his teammate.
why: 很快 describes the manner of the verb 跑到, so 地 before the verb is correct, even though 跑得很快 is the other common pattern.

q: 她很小心___把球放在桌子上。
zh: 她很小心地把球放在桌子上。
py: tā hěn xiǎo xīn de bǎ qiú fàng zài zhuō zi shàng
en: She very carefully put the ball on the table.
why: The describing phrase 很小心 comes before the verb phrase 把球放在桌子上, so 地 joins them.

s: 她很好地踢足球，大家都喜欢看她的比赛。
s_py: tā hěn hǎo de tī zú qiú dà jiā dōu xǐ huān kàn tā de bǐ sài
zh: 她踢足球踢得很好，大家都喜欢看她的比赛。
py: tā tī zú qiú tī de hěn hǎo dà jiā dōu xǐ huān kàn tā de bǐ sài
en: She plays football well, and everybody likes to watch her matches.
why: English 'well' judges how she plays, so Chinese puts it after the verb with 得 and repeats the verb. 很好地踢 is not said.

q: 观众们整齐___站起来，为获胜的队员鼓掌。
zh: 观众们整齐地站起来，为获胜的队员鼓掌。
py: guān zhòng men zhěng qí de zhàn qǐ lái wèi huò shèng de duì yuán gǔ zhǎng
en: The spectators stood up in unison to applaud the winning players.
why: 整齐 describes how they stood up and a verb follows, so 地. 得 would need 整齐 to be the base of a result.

q: 他们热情___告诉我怎么去火车站。
zh: 他们热情地告诉我怎么去火车站。
py: tā men rè qíng de gào sù wǒ zěn me qù huǒ chē zhàn
en: They enthusiastically told me how to get to the train station.
why: 热情 describes how they told me, and 告诉 is a verb, so 地. 得 would need 告诉 on its left instead.

q: 这个城市有很多干净___街道。
zh: 这个城市有很多干净的街道。
py: zhè ge chéng shì yǒu hěn duō gān jìng de jiē dào
en: This city has many clean streets.
why: 干净 describes 街道, a noun, so 的. 得 would need a verb before it and a judgement after it, which this phrase does not have.

q: 每天早上在河边打太极拳___老人们，都住在这个小区。
zh: 每天早上在河边打太极拳的老人们，都住在这个小区。
py: měi tiān zǎo shàng zài hé biān dǎ tài jí quán de lǎo rén men dōu zhù zài zhè ge xiǎo qū
en: The old people who do tai chi by the river every morning all live in this neighbourhood.
why: The long clause describes the noun 老人们, so 的 closes it. 打太极拳 is verb + object, and 得 could not attach after the object anyway.

zh: 外面冷得我们都不想出门。
py: wài miàn lěng de wǒ men dōu bù xiǎng chū mén
en: It is so cold outside that none of us wants to go out.
why: 冷 + 得 + a result clause with its own subject 我们. 得 comes right after 冷.

q: 骑自行车去上班___人越来越多了。
zh: 骑自行车去上班的人越来越多了。
py: qí zì xíng chē qù shàng bān de rén yuè lái yuè duō le
en: More and more people ride bikes to work.
why: 骑自行车去上班 describes the noun 人, so the clause takes 的. 地 would require a verb to follow, but 人 is a noun.

s: 穿蓝衣服得那个人是我们的教练。
s_py: chuān lán yī fú de nà ge rén shì wǒ men de jiào liàn
zh: 穿蓝衣服的那个人是我们的教练。
py: chuān lán yī fú de nà ge rén shì wǒ men de jiào liàn
en: The person wearing blue is our coach.
why: 穿蓝衣服 describes the person 那个人, so the joint is 的. 得 never joins a clause to a noun phrase.

q: 地铁里人多___我们都挤不上去。
zh: 地铁里人多得我们都挤不上去。
py: dì tiě lǐ rén duō de wǒ men dōu jǐ bù shàng qù
en: The metro was so crowded that we could not squeeze on.
why: 人多 states a condition, and 我们都挤不上去 is the result. Adjective + 得 + result clause, so 得.

q: 他每天都努力___练习游泳。
zh: 他每天都努力地练习游泳。
py: tā měi tiān dōu nǔ lì de liàn xí yóu yǒng
en: He practises swimming hard every day.
why: 努力 now comes before the verb 练习, so 地. 得 would need 努力 to be a verb or adjective that the next words comment on.

q: 她认真___看地图。
zh: 她认真地看地图。
py: tā rèn zhēn de kàn dì tú
en: She looks at the map carefully.
why: 认真 describes the manner of the verb 看, so 地 sits before it. 得 follows a verb and would need 看 on the left of the gap.

q: 地图太小了，我们看___清楚路。
zh: 地图太小了，我们看不清楚路。
py: dì tú tài xiǎo le wǒ men kàn bù qīng chǔ lù
en: The map is too small; we can't see the road clearly.
why: The map is too small, so the result is 'cannot'. 看不清楚 replaces 得 with 不; 看得清楚 would say we can.

zh: 我喜欢小王拍的照片。
py: wǒ xǐ huān xiǎo wáng pāi de zhào piān
en: I like the photos Xiao Wang took.
why: The clause 小王拍 describes the noun 照片, so 的 comes after 拍 and before 照片.

q: 他说得太快了，我一句都听___懂。
zh: 他说得太快了，我一句都听不懂。
py: tā shuō de tài kuài le wǒ yī jù dōu tīng bù dǒng
en: He spoke too fast and I couldn't understand a single sentence.
why: 一句都 is a negative-sense phrase, so the form must be the 'cannot' one: 听不懂. 听得懂 would assert that I understood.

s: 今天热得我不想去公园。
s_py: jīn tiān rè de wǒ bù xiǎng qù gōng yuán
zh: 今天热得我不想去公园。
py: jīn tiān rè de wǒ bù xiǎng qù gōng yuán
en: It's so hot today that I don't want to go to the park.
why: 热 + 得 + a clause with its own subject 我 is the 'so ... that' pattern. Correct as it stands.

q: 小王开车___很小心。
zh: 小王开车开得很小心。
py: xiǎo wáng kāi chē kāi de hěn xiǎo xīn
en: Xiao Wang drives very carefully.
why: 开车 is verb + object, so the verb 开 is repeated before 得. Putting 得 after 车 is the classic mistake.

q: 你说___对。
zh: 你说得对。
py: nǐ shuō de duì
en: You're right.
why: 说 is the verb and 对 is the judgement of what was said, so 得. 地 would need a verb after it, and 对 is an adjective.

q: 今天的比赛打___很精彩。
zh: 今天的比赛打得很精彩。
py: jīn tiān de bǐ sài dǎ de hěn jīng cǎi
en: Today's match was played very excitingly.
why: 打 is the verb and 很精彩 is the comment on how the match was played, so 得. Nothing noun-like follows, so 的 is out.

q: 这条街上的车多___我们等了十分钟才过了马路。
zh: 这条街上的车多得我们等了十分钟才过了马路。
py: zhè tiáo jiē shàng de chē duō de wǒ men děng le shí fēn zhōng cái guò le mǎ lù
en: There was so much traffic on this street that we waited ten minutes before we could cross.
why: 车多 is a state, and the result is that we had to wait ten minutes. 'So ... that ...' takes 得. 地 would need a verb of manner to follow.

s: 他认真得听教练说话。
s_py: tā rèn zhēn de tīng jiào liàn shuō huà
zh: 他认真地听教练说话。
py: tā rèn zhēn de tīng jiào liàn shuō huà
en: He listens carefully to the coach.
why: 认真 is the manner of 听, a verb that follows, so 地. 得 cannot come before a verb.

q: 他买了一双很舒服___运动鞋。
zh: 他买了一双很舒服的运动鞋。
py: tā mǎi le yī shuāng hěn shū fú de yùn dòng xié
en: He bought a pair of very comfortable sports shoes.
why: 很舒服 modifies the noun 运动鞋, so 的 is required. 地 would only fit if a verb came next, as in 舒服地坐着.

q: 这家店的蛋糕卖___很快，下午三点就没有了。
zh: 这家店的蛋糕卖得很快，下午三点就没有了。
py: zhè jiā diàn de dàn gāo mài de hěn kuài xià wǔ sān diǎn jiù méi yǒu le
en: The cakes at this shop sell very fast; by three in the afternoon they are gone.
why: 卖 is the verb and 很快 judges how it sells, so 得. 的 would need a noun, and 地 a verb after the gap.

q: 他练球练___连饭都忘了吃。
zh: 他练球练得连饭都忘了吃。
py: tā liàn qiú liàn de lián fàn dōu wàng le chī
en: He practised so hard that he even forgot to eat.
why: 练球 repeats the verb 练, and 得 follows the second 练. What comes next is the result (连饭都忘了吃), so 得.

zh: 她今天跑得很慢。
py: tā jīn tiān pǎo de hěn màn
en: She ran very slowly today.
why: 得 sits between the verb 跑 and the judgement 很慢. The time word 今天 can come before or after 她.

q: 他昨天踢___特别好，进了两个球。
zh: 他昨天踢得特别好，进了两个球。
py: tā zuó tiān tī de tè bié hǎo jìn le liǎng gè qiú
en: He played especially well yesterday and scored two goals.
why: 踢 + 得 + 特别好 judges his play, and the 进了两个球 clause confirms it. 地 would put the quality before the verb as a manner, which does not fit a judgement.

q: 他打篮球___很好。
zh: 他打篮球打得很好。
py: tā dǎ lán qiú dǎ de hěn hǎo
en: He plays basketball very well.
why: 得 must follow a verb directly. With the object 篮球 already after 打, the verb is repeated: 打篮球打得很好. 打篮球得 attaches 得 to the object.

q: 这种篮球在附近的商店买___到。
zh: 这种篮球在附近的商店买得到。
py: zhè zhǒng lán qiú zài fù jìn de shāng diàn mǎi de dào
en: You can buy this kind of basketball at the shops nearby.
why: 买得到 is verb + 得 + result: 'can be bought'. 不 would reverse the meaning. 地 would need a verb after it.

q: 这是一个很清楚___路线图，一看就明白。
zh: 这是一个很清楚的路线图，一看就明白。
py: zhè shì yī gè hěn qīng chǔ de lù xiàn tú yī kàn jiù míng bái
en: This is a very clear route map; you understand it at a glance.
why: 路线图 is a noun, so the description 很清楚 takes 的. The same word before a verb would be 清楚地.

q: 老师说话说___很清楚，我们都听得懂。
zh: 老师说话说得很清楚，我们都听得懂。
py: lǎo shī shuō huà shuō de hěn qīng chǔ wǒ men dōu tīng de dǒng
en: The teacher speaks very clearly and we all understand.
why: 说话说 + 得 + 很清楚 judges how the teacher speaks. 地 would go in front of a verb, but 很清楚 follows the verb.

q: 我累___不想走路了。
zh: 我累得不想走路了。
py: wǒ lèi de bù xiǎng zǒu lù le
en: I'm so tired I don't want to walk any more.
why: 累 is a state and 不想走路了 is the result of it, so 得 links them. 地 would turn 累 into a manner of walking, which is not the meaning.

q: 附近新开了一家非常热闹___咖啡馆，周末常常坐满了人。
zh: 附近新开了一家非常热闹的咖啡馆，周末常常坐满了人。
py: fù jìn xīn kāi le yī jiā fēi cháng rè nào de kā fēi guǎn zhōu mò cháng cháng zuò mǎn le rén
en: A very lively cafe has newly opened nearby, and on weekends it is often full of people.
why: 热闹 describes the noun 咖啡馆 right after the gap, so 的. 热闹得 would need a result clause, and 地 a verb, neither of which follows.

q: 我哥哥游泳___特别快。
zh: 我哥哥游泳游得特别快。
py: wǒ gē gē yóu yǒng yóu de tè bié kuài
en: My older brother swims especially fast.
why: 游泳 is verb + object, so only 游 is repeated: 游泳游得. 游泳得 attaches 得 to the object noun 泳.

s: 他打篮球得很好。
s_py: tā dǎ lán qiú de hěn hǎo
zh: 他打篮球打得很好。
py: tā dǎ lán qiú dǎ de hěn hǎo
en: He plays basketball very well.
why: 得 cannot follow the object 篮球; the verb 打 must be repeated before 得. Without the repeated verb the judgement hangs on a noun.

q: 教练严肃___对我们说：“明天别迟到。”
zh: 教练严肃地对我们说：“明天别迟到。”
py: jiào liàn yán sù de duì wǒ men shuō míng tiān bié chí dào
en: The coach said to us seriously, "Do not be late tomorrow."
why: 严肃 is the manner of speaking and the verb 对我们说 follows, so 地. 严肃得 would need a result clause to follow.

q: 我喜欢这家很便宜___小饭馆。
zh: 我喜欢这家很便宜的小饭馆。
py: wǒ xǐ huān zhè jiā hěn pián yi de xiǎo fàn guǎn
en: I like this very cheap little restaurant.
why: The noun 小饭馆 follows the gap and 很便宜 describes it, so 的. 地 would introduce a verb, which is not here.

q: 那位年轻___教练对每个队员都很耐心。
zh: 那位年轻的教练对每个队员都很耐心。
py: nà wèi nián qīng de jiào liàn duì měi gè duì yuán dōu hěn nài xīn
en: That young coach is patient with every player.
why: 年轻 is a plain adjective in front of the noun 教练, so 的. The later verb phrase is a separate predicate and does not change the position of the gap.

q: 在公园跑步___人很多。
zh: 在公园跑步的人很多。
py: zài gōng yuán pǎo bù de rén hěn duō
en: There are many people jogging in the park.
why: 在公园跑步 describes who the 人 are, so the clause is linked to the noun with 的. 地 would put a verb after it.

q: 弟弟跳___不太高。
zh: 弟弟跳得不太高。
py: dì di tiào de bù tài gāo
en: My younger brother doesn't jump very high.
why: The verb 跳 is followed by a judgement 不太高, so 得. The 不 belongs on the judgement, never in front of the verb.

q: 她有一双大大___眼睛，很喜欢打羽毛球。
zh: 她有一双大大的眼睛，很喜欢打羽毛球。
py: tā yǒu yī shuāng dà dà de yǎn jīng hěn xǐ huān dǎ yǔ máo qiú
en: She has a pair of big eyes and likes playing badminton.
why: 大大 describes the noun 眼睛, so the doubled adjective takes 的. Doubling does not force 地.

q: 请你仔细___听路线。
zh: 请你仔细地听路线。
py: qǐng nǐ zǐ xì de tīng lù xiàn
en: Please listen carefully to the route.
why: 仔细 tells how to 听, so 仔细 + 地 + verb. 得 would require a verb or adjective before it with a judgement after.

s: 他是一个跑得很快的运动员。
s_py: tā shì yí gè pǎo de hěn kuài de yùn dòng yuán
zh: 他是一个跑得很快的运动员。
py: tā shì yī gè pǎo de hěn kuài de yùn dòng yuán
en: He is an athlete who runs very fast.
why: 跑得很快 is the clause, and 的 joins it to the noun 运动员. Both de are correct.

q: 你刚才问___那家银行就在前面。
zh: 你刚才问的那家银行就在前面。
py: nǐ gāng cái wèn de nà jiā yín háng jiù zài qián miàn
en: The bank you just asked about is right ahead.
why: 你刚才问 is a clause that identifies the noun 那家银行, so 的 joins them. A verb after the gap would be needed for 地.

q: 他骑自行车___不太稳。
zh: 他骑自行车骑得不太稳。
py: tā qí zì xíng chē qí de bù tài wěn
en: He doesn't ride a bike very steadily.
why: With the object 自行车 after 骑, the verb must come back before 得: 骑自行车骑得不太稳. 得 alone would follow the object.

q: 他饿___连跑步的力气都没有了。
zh: 他饿得连跑步的力气都没有了。
py: tā è de lián pǎo bù de lì qì dōu méi yǒu le
en: He was so hungry he did not even have the strength to run.
why: 饿 is a state, and 连跑步的力气都没有了 is how far it went, so 得. 饿 cannot be the manner of any action here, so 地 fails.
